dtype_contract: BF16 inputs, BF16 recurrent state, bitwise-equal state transition and gated RMSNorm output
candidate: one Triton program per value head; four sequential BV32 state slices followed by in-launch 128-wide gated RMSNorm

architectural_change.stock: 64 recurrent programs plus a separate gated RMSNorm launch per GDN layer
architectural_change.intended_gain: load q/k and recurrent scalars once per head and remove one producer-consumer launch boundary
architectural_change.measured_cost: four state slices become serial within each head, reducing parallelism

uncaptured_python_submission.interpretation: allocator and host-submission artifact; not representative of vLLM decode

cache_evicted_paired_single_launch.interpretation: independent confirmation that the candidate does not win

closed_family: single-program-per-head sequential recurrence plus gated normalization
reopen_conditions: A design preserves four BV32 tiles of parallelism while providing an exact head-wide reduction boundary.
A CUDA or warp-specialized implementation demonstrates state and output equality before full-model integration.
The vLLM execution path no longer uses CUDA Graph replay, making host launch and allocation overhead material again.
claim_limit: This rejects one ownership/dataflow design; it does not prove every recurrent-state layout or convolution-recurrence fusion is suboptimal.
